claim: LARP4 binds poly(A) and PABP.
source: La-related protein-4 (LARP4) binds poly(A) and PABP.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known property of LARP4.

claim: LARP4 mRNA contains a translation-dependent, coding region determinant (CRD) of instability that limits its expression.
source: LARP4 mRNA contains a translation-dependent, coding region determinant (CRD) of instability that limits its expression.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The CRD comprises <10% of LARP4 codons.
source: Although the CRD comprises <10% of LARP4 codons, the mRNA levels vary >20 fold with synonymous CRD substitutions that accommodate tRNA dynamics.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data showing the CRD spans codons 287-358 of a 724 codon protein.

claim: LARP4 mRNA levels vary >20 fold with synonymous CRD substitutions that accommodate tRNA dynamics.
source: Although the CRD comprises <10% of LARP4 codons, the mRNA levels vary >20 fold with synonymous CRD substitutions that accommodate tRNA dynamics.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by Figure 3c showing the range of expression from different CS constructs.

claim: Overexpression of the most limiting tRNA increases LARP4 levels.
source: Separately, overexpression of the most limiting tRNA increases LARP4 levels and reveals its functional activity, net lengthening of the PATs of heterologous mRNAs with concomitant stabilization, including ribosomal protein (RP) mRNAs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: Overexpression of the most limiting tRNA reveals LARP4's functional activity of net lengthening of the PATs of heterologous mRNAs with concomitant stabilization, including ribosomal protein (RP) mRNAs.
source: Separately, overexpression of the most limiting tRNA increases LARP4 levels and reveals its functional activity, net lengthening of the PATs of heterologous mRNAs with concomitant stabilization, including ribosomal protein (RP) mRNAs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing mRNA mobility shifts and stability changes.

claim: Genetic deletion of cellular LARP4 decreases PAT length and RPmRNA stability.
source: Genetic deletion of cellular LARP4 decreases PAT length and RPmRNA stability.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by experiments with LARP4 knockout MEFs shown in Figure 7.

claim: LARP4 activity requires its PABP-interaction domain.
source: This LARP4 activity requires its PABP-interaction domain and the RNA-binding module which we show is sensitive to poly(A) 3'-termini, consistent with protection from deadenylation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by mutant analysis in Figure 4b showing reduced activity with PABP-interaction domain deletions.

claim: LARP4 activity requires its RNA-binding module which is sensitive to poly(A) 3'-termini.
source: This LARP4 activity requires its PABP-interaction domain and the RNA-binding module which we show is sensitive to poly(A) 3'-termini, consistent with protection from deadenylation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by RNA binding data in Figure 8 and mutant analysis in Figure 4b.

claim: LARP4 is a posttranscriptional regulator of ribosomal protein production in mammalian cells.
source: The results indicate that LARP4 is a posttranscriptional regulator of ribosomal protein production in mammalian cells and suggest that this activity can be controlled by tRNA levels.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings showing LARP4 effects on RP mRNA stability and PAT length.

claim: LARP4 activity can be controlled by tRNA levels.
source: The results indicate that LARP4 is a posttranscriptional regulator of ribosomal protein production in mammalian cells and suggest that this activity can be controlled by tRNA levels.
evidence: This is suggested in the abstract and supported by data showing tRNA overexpression increases LARP4 levels and activity.

claim: PAT length is associated with translation efficiency in early development.
source: PAT length is associated with translation efficiency in early development (Subtelny et al., 2014), and for specific mRNAs in somatic cells (Park et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Subtelny et al., 2014.

claim: PAT length is associated with translation efficiency for specific mRNAs in somatic cells.
source: PAT length is associated with translation efficiency in early development (Subtelny et al., 2014), and for specific mRNAs in somatic cells (Park et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Park et al., 2016.

claim: PABP interacts with multiple different proteins involved in mRNA translation and stability.
source: PABP interacts with multiple different proteins involved in mRNA translation and stability (Mangus et al., 2003; Ivanov et al., 2016).

source: Several of these proteins, among which are key factors involved in mRNA 3' exonucleolytic deadenylation, translation initiation and termination, share a similar peptide sequence termed PAM2 that interacts with the C-terminal domain of PABP (Xie et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xie et al., 2014.

claim: Some proteins with a PAM2 sequence including Paips 1 and 2, LARPs 1, 4 and 4B, also harbor other regions that interact with PABP.
source: Some proteins with a PAM2 sequence including Paips 1 and 2, LARPs 1, 4 and 4B, also harbor other regions that interact with PABP (Yang et al., 2011; Tcherkezian et al., 2014; Xie et al., 2014; Fonseca et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yang et al., 2011; Tcherkezian et al., 2014; Xie et al., 2014; Fonseca et al., 2015.

claim: LARPs 1, 4 and 4B associate with translating polyribosomes.

evidence: This is supported by citations to Schäffler et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2011; Tcherkezian et al., 2014; Fonseca et al., 2015.

claim: The 'La module' of the eukaryote-ubiquitous nuclear La protein is comprised of a La motif (LaM) followed by an RNA recognition motif (RRM) that cooperate to form a RNA binding pocket that recognizes the extreme UUU-3'OH termini of RNA polymerase III transcripts and protects them from 3' exonucleases.
source: The 'La module' of the eukaryote-ubiquitous nuclear La protein is comprised of a La motif (LaM) followed by an RNA recognition motif (RRM) that cooperate to form a RNA binding pocket that recognizes the extreme UUU-3'OH termini of RNA polymerase III transcripts and protects them from 3' exonucleases (Bayfield et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bayfield et al., 2010.

claim: The La module has been highly conserved by a few distinct La-related proteins (LARPs) that arose during eukaryotic evolution but diverged in other features of their structure and function.
source: The La module has been highly conserved by a few distinct La-related proteins (LARPs) that arose during eukaryotic evolution but diverged in other features of their structure and function (Bousquet-Antonelli and Deragon, 2009; Maraia et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bousquet-Antonelli and Deragon, 2009; Maraia et al., 2017.

claim: LARPs 1, 4, 4B and 6 are mostly cytoplasmic and associated with mRNAs.
source: Of these, LARPs 1, 4, 4B and 6 are mostly cytoplasmic and associated with mRNAs (Maraia et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Maraia et al., 2017.

claim: Vertebrate LARP6 binds a highly conserved stem-bulge-loop found in the 5' UTRs of three α-collagen mRNAs.

evidence: This is supported by citations to Cai et al., 2010; Martino et al., 2015; Zhang and Stefanovic, 2016.

claim: Details of RNA binding by the La modules of LARPs 1, 4 and 4B, and how such binding may contribute to their activities are largely unknown.
source: Yet, except for vertebrate LARP6 which binds a highly conserved stem-bulge-loop found in the 5' UTRs of three α-collagen mRNAs (Cai et al., 2010; Martino et al., 2015; Zhang and Stefanovic, 2016), details of RNA binding by the La modules of LARPs 1, 4 and 4B, and how such binding may contribute to their activities are largely unknown (Maraia et al., 2017).

evidence: This is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2011.

claim: Full length LARP4B has been shown to bind A-rich, U-containing RNA.
source: The La module-containing N-terminal domain of LARP4 has been shown to bind homopoly(A) whereas its full length homolog, LARP4B has been shown to bind A-rich, U-containing RNA (Yang et al., 2011; Küspert et al., 2015), consistent with key differences in their La motifs (Bayfield et al., 2010; Maraia et al., 2017); their regulation also differs since LARP4 but not 4B mRNA is destabilized by TTP (Mattijssen and Maraia, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yang et al., 2011; Küspert et al., 2015.

claim: LARP4 but not 4B mRNA is destabilized by TTP.
source: The La module-containing N-terminal domain of LARP4 has been shown to bind homopoly(A) whereas its full length homolog, LARP4B has been shown to bind A-rich, U-containing RNA (Yang et al., 2011; Küspert et al., 2015), consistent with key differences in their La motifs (Bayfield et al., 2010; Maraia et al., 2017); their regulation also differs since LARP4 but not 4B mRNA is destabilized by TTP (Mattijssen and Maraia, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mattijssen and Maraia, 2015.

claim: LARP1 appears to bind poly(A) and to stabilize mRNAs containing the 5' terminal oligo pyrimidine (5'TOP) motif.
source: LARP1 appears to bind poly(A) and to stabilize mRNAs containing the 5' terminal oligo pyrimidine (5'TOP) motif (Aoki et al., 2013) which are comprised of mRNAs encoding ribosomal proteins (RP), translation factors, PABP and other proteins (Meyuhas and Kahan, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Aoki et al., 2013.

claim: 5'TOP mRNAs are comprised of mRNAs encoding ribosomal proteins (RP), translation factors, PABP and other proteins.
source: LARP1 appears to bind poly(A) and to stabilize mRNAs containing the 5' terminal oligo pyrimidine (5'TOP) motif (Aoki et al., 2013) which are comprised of mRNAs encoding ribosomal proteins (RP), translation factors, PABP and other proteins (Meyuhas and Kahan, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Meyuhas and Kahan, 2015.

claim: LARP1 is known to have two RNA-binding domains, a La module in its N-terminal half and a C-terminal HEAT motif that directly binds the 5' m7G cap and pyrimidine tract of the 5'TOP motif.
source: LARP1 is known to have two RNA-binding domains, a La module in its N-terminal half (Nykamp et al., 2008) and a C-terminal HEAT motif that directly binds the 5' m7G cap and pyrimidine tract of the 5'TOP motif (Lahr et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Nykamp et al., 2008 and Lahr et al., 2017.

claim: LARP1 may regulate a number of transcripts in addition to the 5'TOP mRNAs.
source: LARP1 may regulate a number of transcripts in addition to the 5'TOP mRNAs (Blagden et al., 2009; Tcherkezian et al., 2014; Fonseca et al., 2015; Mura et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Blagden et al., 2009; Tcherkezian et al., 2014; Fonseca et al., 2015; Mura et al., 2015.

claim: Coding region determinants (CRD) of instability have been found in a small number of mRNAs, including Fos and Myc.
source: Coding region determinants (CRD) of instability have been found in a small number of mRNAs, including Fos and Myc (Lemm and Ross, 2002; Chang et al., 2004) (reviewed in Lee and Gorospe, 2011) and for Fos involves interactions with PABP, translating ribosomes, and deadenylation (reviewed in Chen and Shyu, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lemm and Ross, 2002; Chang et al., 2004.

claim: For Fos, the CRD involves interactions with PABP, translating ribosomes, and deadenylation.
source: Coding region determinants (CRD) of instability have been found in a small number of mRNAs, including Fos and Myc (Lemm and Ross, 2002; Chang et al., 2004) (reviewed in Lee and Gorospe, 2011) and for Fos involves interactions with PABP, translating ribosomes, and deadenylation (reviewed in Chen and Shyu, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chen and Shyu, 2011.

source: Accumulating evidence indicate that the overall fraction of optimal vs. suboptimal codons in a mRNA is a major determinant of mRNA decay in yeast (Presnyak et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Presnyak et al., 2015.

claim: A potential link between mRNA codon use and decay appears more complex in higher eukaryotic cells in which the relatively high content of 3′ UTR-destabilizing elements is a confounding issue.
source: A potential link between mRNA codon use and decay appears more complex in higher eukaryotic cells in which the relatively high content of 3′ UTR-destabilizing elements is a confounding issue (reviewed in Chen and Shyu, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chen and Shyu, 2017.

claim: LARP4 accumulated to much lower levels than any other LARP tested, with LARP4B as the highest.
source: LARP4 accumulated to much lower levels than any other, with LARP4B, a homolog of similar mass (below), as the highest (Figure 1b).

claim: LARP4 mRNA accumulated to the lowest levels among the LARPs tested.
source: Northern blotting showed that LARP4 mRNA accumulated to the lowest levels (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1c northern blot.

claim: LARP4 mRNA was less than LARPs 6 and 4B by ~100 and ~50 fold respectively.
source: LARP4 mRNA was less than LARPs 6 and 4B by ~100 and ~50 fold respectively (Figure 1d), likely reflective of different stabilities of their coding regions.
evidence: This is stated in the text and quantified in Figure 1d.

claim: Codons 287–358 of LARP4 mRNA contain a coding region determinant (CRD) that is inhibitory to expression.
source: These data suggested a region within codons 287–358 as inhibitory to expression, which was confirmed by the internal deletion construct, Δ287–358 that was expressed at levels nearly as high as 359–724 and much higher than 1–724 and 1–430 (Figure 1g). The differences in protein levels were generally reflected by the mRNAs (Figure 1f,g lower). Thus, codons 287–358 of LARP4 mRNA contain a coding region determinant (CRD) that is inhibitory to expression.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figures 1f and 1g showing deletion constructs.

claim: The CRD comprises a tract of <10% of the ORF length that encodes part of LARP4 protein that is important for interaction with PABP, termed the PABP-binding motif (PBM).
source: This comprises a tract of <10% of the ORF length that encodes part of LARP4 protein that is important for interaction with PABP, termed the PABP-binding motif (PBM) (Yang et al., 2011) (below).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citation to Yang et al., 2011.

claim: When the CRD is placed in the ORF preceding the stop codon, it leads to significantly lower t=0 mRNA levels compared to placement after the stop codon.
source: When preceding the stop codon, the CRD led to t = 0 levels that were significantly lower as compared to placement after the stop (Figure 1i upper panel, lanes 1 and 6).

claim: The CRD produced more instability as part of the ORF as compared to following the stop codon.

source: A synonymous codon-swapped (CS) CRD sequence inserted in the βG CDS increased reporter mRNA levels and half-life relative to the WT CRD in the CDS (Figure 1i,j).

claim: A +2 frameshift CRD largely reversed the inhibitory effect of the WT CRD.
source: Similar to CS, the +2 FS largely reversed the inhibitory effect of the WT CRD (Figure 1k).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1k.

source: The WT-CRD decreased LARP4B-CRD-WT levels relative to LARP4B WT (Figure 2b, lanes 5, 4).

evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 2b and 2c.

claim: The LARP4 CRD is recognized as inhibitory when transferred to a heterologous mRNA.
source: Importantly, the CS CRD rescued the negative effect of WT-CRD (Figure 2b, lanes 6, 5); see quantitation in Figure 2c. Thus, the LARP4 CRD is recognized as inhibitory when transferred to a heterologous mRNA.

source: The native 3'UTR of LARP4 mRNA is 4.2 kb and contains A+U rich elements controlled by TNFα via TTP (Mattijssen and Maraia, 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citation to Mattijssen and Maraia, 2015.

evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figures 2d and 2e.

claim: The CRD is highly biased in its use of each of the three weak wobble codons (Asn AAU, Phe UUU, Tyr UAU).

source: The other noteworthy finding resulted from codon swaps of weak, all-A+U wobble codons to their stronger synonymous codons with a C in the third position. In these cases the new codon is decoded by the same tRNA but using a direct match anticodon wobble G34. These data revealed that wobble decoding of weak codons can be a significant determinant of suboptimality (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Translation dependency and the instability component of the CRD can be uncoupled.
source: This suggests that translation dependency and the instability component of the CRD can be uncoupled and that reversing the latter may require more than an increase in the levels of a single tRNA.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Over expression of the lowest abundance tRNA, tRNAThrUGU, increased production of LARP4 and GFP from transfected plasmids.
source: A striking finding was demonstration that over expression of the lowest abundance, tRNAThrUGU, increased production of LARP4 and GFP from transfected plasmids (Figures 3g–h and 5b).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figures 3g-h and 5b.

claim: This tRNA overexpression was accompanied by a shift of the corresponding mRNAs to heavier polysome fractions, presumably reflective of greater ribosome occupancy.
source: As expected, this was accompanied by a shift of the corresponding mRNAs to heavier polysome fractions, presumably reflective of greater ribosome occupancy (Figure 6g–i).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figures 6g-i.

claim: This tRNA overexpression activity was specific since over expression of other low (or high) abundance tRNAs including tRNAThrCGU or tRNATyrGUA did not increase LARP4 or GFP production.
source: This was a robust activity that was specific since over expression of other low (or high) abundance tRNAs including tRNAThrCGU or tRNATyrGUA did not increase LARP4 or GFP production (Figure 3e,f and data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figures 3e and 3f.

claim: 14 of the 15 threonines in the codon-optimized GFP construct are encoded by ACC codons and these require wobble decoding because there is no tRNA with a GGU anticodon.
source: We note that 14 of the 15 threonines in the codon-optimized GFP construct (Haas et al., 1996) are encoded by ACC codons and that these require wobble decoding because there is no tRNA with a GGU anticodon (Table 1) (Gogakos et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Table 1 and citations.

claim: In yeast, tRNAThrUGU carries the ncm5U modification.
source: While the wobble base modification status of human tRNAThrUGU has not been reported, in yeast it carries the ncm5U modification (Johansson et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Johansson et al., 2008.

claim: The ncm5U modified base on tRNAProUGG has been shown to wobble decode the Pro codon with C in the wobble position.
source: This same ncm5U modified base on tRNAProUGG has been shown to wobble decode the Pro codon with C in the wobble position (Johansson et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Johansson et al., 2008.

claim: Although there is a large difference in the instability of the LARP4-WT and LARP4-CS-Tyr mRNAs as the latter accumulates to ~12 fold higher than the former, we do not know the source, in vivo kinetics, cell biology, specific factors involved nor the mechanism by which the CRD mediates the effect.
source: While there is a large difference in the instability of the LARP4-WT and LARP4-CS-Tyr mRNAs as the latter accumulates to ~12 fold higher than the former (Figure 3c), we note that we do not know the source, in vivo kinetics, cell biology, specific factors involved nor the mechanism by which the CRD mediates the effect.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an acknowledgment of limitations.

claim: The different LARP4 truncation and deletion construct mRNAs containing or lacking the CRD would appear to have similar apparent translation efficiencies because the relative amounts of the mRNAs more or less match the relative amounts of proteins produced.
source: As was evident from our early analysis of Figure 1e–g, the different LARP4 truncation and deletion construct mRNAs containing or lacking the CRD would appear to have similar apparent translation efficiencies because the relative amounts of the mRNAs more or less match the relative amounts of proteins produced (Figure 1e–g).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an observation from the data.

source: Moreover, this trend of match between relative amounts of mRNAs and proteins produced was maintained by the synonymous CS constructs analyzed in Figure 3a–c (and data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an observation from the data.

claim: Although LARP4-WT mRNA accumulates to ~12 fold lower levels than LARP4-CS-Tyr mRNA, the LARP4-WT mRNA that does survive appears to exhibit translational efficiency that is only modestly lower than LARP4-CS-Tyr mRNA based on polysome profile distributions.
source: It is also interesting to consider that although LARP4-WT mRNA accumulates to ~12 fold lower levels than LARP4-CS-Tyr mRNA, the LARP4-WT mRNA that does survive appears to exhibit translational efficiency that is only modestly lower than LARP4-CS-Tyr mRNA based on polysome profile distributions (Figure 6b–e).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an observation from the data.

claim: The data are consistent with some type of quality control mechanism that leads to decay of a large fraction of the LARP4-WT mRNA because it has suboptimal codons.
source: The data are consistent with some type of quality control mechanism that leads to decay of a large fraction of the LARP4-WT mRNA because it has suboptimal codons (Radhakrishnan and Green, 2016) (see Brule and Grayhack, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to Radhakrishnan and Green, 2016 and Brule and Grayhack, 2017.

claim: There was comparably robust translation through the CRD regions of both LARP4-WT(1-358) and LARP4-CS-Tyr(1-358) synthetic mRNAs in vitro.
source: However, there was comparably robust translation through the CRD regions of both of the synthetic mRNAs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The in vitro translation results suggest the possibility that the mechanism controlling the synonymous codon-specific differential expression/decay of LARP4-WT and -CS-Tyr in cells is coupled to transcription or another nuclear event(s) or process that is not faithfully executed during in vitro translation in extract of synthetic mRNAs.
source: The in vitro translation results suggest among other things the possibility that the mechanism controlling the synonymous codon-specific differential expression/decay of LARP4-WT and -CS-Tyr in cells is coupled to transcription or another nuclear event(s) or process that is not faithfully executed during in vitro translation in extract of synthetic mRNAs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a possible interpretation of the in vitro translation results.

claim: Such a possibility would be consistent with a quality control mechanism that is operational in vivo.
source: Such a possibility would be consistent with a quality control mechanism that is operational in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation.

claim: Sensitivity of single stranded poly(A) RNA to 3' end binding by LARP4 had remained untested prior to this work.
source: We also note that sensitivity of single stranded poly(A) RNA to 3' end binding by LARP4 had remained untested.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as context for the new findings.

claim: LARP4 exhibits sensitivity to the 3' end of poly(A) in a manner similar to that of the RNA binding pocket of La protein during RNA 3' end sequestration.
source: We used in vitro RNA binding to reveal that LARP4 exhibits sensitivity to the 3' end of poly(A) in a manner similar to that of the RNA binding pocket of La protein during RNA 3' end sequestration (Teplova et al., 2006; Kotik-Kogan et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to Teplova et al., 2006; Kotik-Kogan et al., 2008.

claim: This apparent similarity in 3' end sensitivity occurs despite other significant differences in RNA recognition by La and LARP4 including oligo(U) vs. oligo(A) specificity, RNA length requirements.
source: We note that this apparent similarity occurs despite other significant differences in RNA recognition by La and LARP4 including oligo(U) vs. oligo(A) specificity, RNA length requirements (Yang et al., 2011), and that the molecular and structural bases of these for LARP4 are unknown (reviewed in Maraia et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to Yang et al., 2011 and Maraia et al., 2017.

claim: The molecular and structural bases of RNA recognition differences between La and LARP4 are unknown.
source: We note that this apparent similarity occurs despite other significant differences in RNA recognition by La and LARP4 including oligo(U) vs. oligo(A) specificity, RNA length requirements (Yang et al., 2011), and that the molecular and structural bases of these for LARP4 are unknown (reviewed in Maraia et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to Maraia et al., 2017.

claim: Future experiments toward understanding how the PABP-interaction domains of LARP4 cooperate with its La module will be necessary to better understand its activity for PAT lengthening.
source: In any case, future experiments toward understanding how the PABP-interaction domains of LARP4 cooperate with its La module will be necessary to better understand its activity for PAT lengthening.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a future direction.

claim: In the current working model, the La module of LARP4 would bind poly(A), and its PBM and PAM2 would bind PABP, the latter of which also binds the PAT.
source: In the current working model, the La module of LARP4 would bind poly(A), and its PBM and PAM2 would bind PABP, the latter of which also binds the PAT.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a proposed model.

claim: Presumably, the LARP4 PAM2 would serve to compete with or displace from PABP, the PAM2-containing deadenylases which function as 3' exonucleases.
source: Presumably, the LARP4 PAM2 would serve to compete with or displace from PABP, the PAM2-containing deadenylases which function as 3' exonucleases.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a proposed mechanism.

claim: MEFs derived from LARP4 gene-deleted KO embryos were shown to bear RPmRNAs with shorter PAT length and faster decay than in WT MEFs.
source: MEFs derived from LARP4 gene-deleted KO embryos created for this study were shown to bear RPmRNAs with shorter PAT length and faster decay than in WT MEFs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: The mRNA-PAT length maintenance mediated by LARP4 characterized here was mostly for the highly abundant RPmRNAs.
source: The mRNA-PAT length maintenance mediated by LARP4 characterized here was mostly for the highly abundant RPmRNAs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: LARP4 activity to increase PAT length was not limited to RPmRNAs.
source: However, we wish to emphasize that LARP4 activity to increase PAT length was not limited to these mRNAs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion to clarify the scope of LARP4 activity.

claim: Elevation of cellular LARP4 levels in response to increase in limiting tRNA or other means led to PAT lengthening and stabilization of βG-TNFα-ARE mRNA whose ARE directs deadenylation.
source: Elevation of cellular LARP4 levels in response to increase in limiting tRNA or other means led to PAT lengthening and stabilization of βG-TNFα-ARE mRNA whose ARE directs deadenylation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: LARP4 would appear to differ from other mRNA stabilizing proteins which generally target lower abundance and transiently expressed mRNAs that are relatively unstable in their basal state and regulated through their 3'UTRs.
source: Yet LARP4 would appear to differ from other mRNA stabilizing proteins which generally target lower abundance and transiently expressed mRNAs that are relatively unstable in their basal state (as compared to RPmRNAs) and regulated through their 3'UTRs, e.g., via AREs that indirectly modulate PAT metabolism via trans-acting factors (Chen and Shyu, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citation to Chen and Shyu, 2017.

claim: LARP4 differs because it binds directly to poly(A), the RPmRNAs are abundant and contain relatively very short 3' UTRs that are generally believed to be non-regulatory in the conventional sense.
source: According to the model derived from our data, LARP4 differs because it binds directly to poly(A), the RPmRNAs are abundant and contain relatively very short 3' UTRs that are generally believed to be non-regulatory in the conventional sense.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the data.

claim: LARP4 would appear to be a general factor that is more directly involved in PAT length maintenance.
source: Thus, LARP4 would appear to be a general factor that is more directly involved in PAT length maintenance.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion.

claim: The RPmRNAs comprise a substantial fraction of cellular mRNA in proliferating cells, and are critical and tightly regulated, including under growth control.
source: The RPmRNAs comprise a substantial fraction of cellular mRNA in proliferating cells, and ﻿are critical and tightly regulated, including under growth control.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as background knowledge.

claim: LARP4B and LARP1 also exhibit mRNA PAT net lengthening activity.
source: Our data demonstrated mRNA PAT net lengthening activity for two other La module proteins, LARP4B and LARP1 (Figure 4 and 9), the latter of which is a regulator of ribosome biogenesis and a pro-cancer protein (Aoki et al., 2013; Tcherkezian et al., 2014; Fonseca et al., 2015; Lahr et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figures 4 and 9 and citations.

claim: LARP1 is a regulator of ribosome biogenesis and a pro-cancer protein.
source: Our data demonstrated mRNA PAT net lengthening activity for two other La module proteins, LARP4B and LARP1 (Figure 4 and 9), the latter of which is a regulator of ribosome biogenesis and a pro-cancer protein (Aoki et al., 2013; Tcherkezian et al., 2014; Fonseca et al., 2015; Lahr et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Aoki et al., 2013; Tcherkezian et al., 2014; Fonseca et al., 2015; Lahr et al., 2017.

claim: Neither over expression of La protein, a significant fraction of which is cytoplasmic, nor LARPs 6 or 7, exhibited PAT lengthening activity even when accumulated at higher levels than LARP4-WT and -CS-R.
source: By contrast, neither over expression of La protein, a significant fraction of which is cytoplasmic, nor LARPs 6 or 7, exhibited this activity even when accumulated at higher levels than LARP4-WT and -CS-R (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion based on unpublished data.

claim: LARP4B contains a PAM2 and a separate PBM.
source: LARP4B contains a PAM2 and a separate PBM (Bayfield et al., 2010; Schäffler et al., 2010), and recent data identified a PAM2 candidate in LARP1 (Fonseca et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bayfield et al., 2010; Schäffler et al., 2010.

claim: Recent data identified a PAM2 candidate in LARP1.
source: LARP4B contains a PAM2 and a separate PBM (Bayfield et al., 2010; Schäffler et al., 2010), and recent data identified a PAM2 candidate in LARP1 (Fonseca et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Fonseca et al., 2015.

claim: LARP1 is a central factor in the regulation of translation of RPmRNAs in response to nutrition-related signals by controlling their repression which is mediated by its DM15 domain which binds their 5'TOP motif.
source: LARP1 is a central factor in the regulation of translation of RPmRNAs in response to nutrition-related signals by controlling their repression which is mediated by its DM15 domain which binds their 5'TOP motif (Lahr et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lahr et al., 2017.

source: However, a recognized part of LARP1 activity in regulation is RPmRNA stabilization (Tcherkezian et al., 2014; Fonseca et al., 2015) and some data suggested that this may be mediated via binding to the 3′ terminus of the PAT (Aoki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Tcherkezian et al., 2014; Fonseca et al., 2015.

claim: Some data suggested that LARP1-mediated RPmRNA stabilization may be mediated via binding to the 3′ terminus of the PAT.
source: However, a recognized part of LARP1 activity in regulation is RPmRNA stabilization (Tcherkezian et al., 2014; Fonseca et al., 2015) and some data suggested that this may be mediated via binding to the 3′ terminus of the PAT (Aoki et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Aoki et al., 2013.

claim: LARP1 stabilized/increased accumulation of βG-TNFα-ARE mRNA with accompanying mobility shift and it similarly shifted GFP mRNA which was shown to result from PAT lengthening.
source: Our data showed that LARP1 stabilized/increased accumulation of βG-TNFα-ARE mRNA with accompanying mobility shift and it similarly shifted GFP mRNA which was shown to result from PAT lengthening (Figure 9).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 9.

source: As neither of these mRNAs bear a 5'TOP motif, the data suggest that the PAT-mediated mRNA stability may be a separate activity of LARP1.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the data.

claim: PAT-mediated mRNA stability by LARP1 may be uncoupled from translation repression including when LARP1 is over-expressed as occurs in certain cancers and associates with non-TOP mRNAs.
source: This further suggests that PAT-mediated mRNA stability by LARP1 may be uncoupled from translation repression including when LARP1 is over-expressed as occurs in certain cancers and associates with non-TOP mRNAs (Mura et al., 2015; Stavraka and Blagden, 2015; Hopkins et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations to Mura et al., 2015; Stavraka and Blagden, 2015; Hopkins et al., 2016.

source: However, while LARP1 contributes to RPmRNA translation as a central negative regulator, the present work suggests that LARP4 may be more of a constitutive positive factor in the control of RPmRNA homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the work.

source: Finally, an intriguing aspect of this work is that tRNA availability might control or tune LARP4 activity levels.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation based on the findings.
